newsitem.title: CHINA: China '97 corn prices seen depressed - newsletter.
newsitem.headline: China '97 corn prices seen depressed - newsletter.

text.p: China's domestic corn prices are likely to remain under pressure next year because of a projected bumper harvest in 1996 and weak demand, an official newsletter said in an edition seen in Beijing on Monday.
"We can say with certainty that supply will continue to outstrip demand in domestic corn markets in 1997," said the China and Overseas Grain, Oil and Feed Information newsletter.

"If the government does not take proper macro-control measures, domestic corn prices are unlikely to recover from their current low levels," said the authoritative newsletter, published by the State Grain Reserve Bureau.
It said the price of corn in a key growing region in the northeast was 1,250 yuan per tonne, down nearly 18 percent from a year ago.
China's corn output is expected to hit 114 million tonnes in 1996 mainly because of a relatively big increase in acreage under corn this year, the newsletter said.
China produced 111.99 million tonnes of corn in 1995, up 12.71 million tonnes from 1994, official figures showed.
Domestic prices have been sluggish since late 1995 because of oversupply created by the bumper corn harvest and a sharp surge in corn imports in 1995, the newsletter said.
Corn imports rose to 5.18 million tonnes in 1995 from nearly zero the previous year, customs figures showed.

China officially banned corn exports in late 1994 in a bid to curb rising domestic prices. Prices have since fallen but there has been no sign of government willingness to allow exports except for what it calls special circumstances.
China's corn exports plunged by 98.7 percent to 110,000 tonnes in 1995.

Meanwhile, domestic demand for corn has been weak mainly because of falling production of animal feed, the newsletter said. Feed output in China fell by 8.46 percent in the first seven months of this year from the same period of 1995.
